title: Ines and the Signal
premise: Paloma Sterling tends the last terraformed garden on a forgotten moon, maintaining a beacon that broadcasts a false signal of an uninhabitable world. When the deep-space ship Vesper returns with its crew aged backward into children, Paloma learns the beacon was built to hide this colony from two rival fleets poised for war—and that the signal is failing. To keep the lie alive, Paloma must impersonate the dead engineer who designed it, falling in love with the Vesper's de-aged captain, Ines, who carries fragmented memories of the truth. As both fleets converge on the moon, Paloma must choose between preserving the deception that keeps peace and revealing the garden's existence; in the end, Paloma broadcasts the truth and the garden itself becomes neutral ground where the fleets negotiate, while Ines, restored to adulthood by the moon's temporal field, chooses to stay.
about_author: Paloma Okafor is a former botanist who spent a decade restoring wetlands before turning to fiction about worlds worth saving. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps a greenhouse of plants grown from seeds salvaged from old colony missions.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Establishes daily life tending the terraforming garden and maintaining the mysterious beacon alone on the moon Meridian. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by loneliness and the ache of working for people who may never come.

chapters.title: Beacon Log 4,412
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers an encrypted maintenance log from the beacon's designer, Engineer Adeyemi Sol, written in a personal code. Emotional beat: curiosity kindling into unease as the log hints the beacon hides something, not something.

chapters.title: A Light in the Dark
chapters.summary: Paloma detects an approaching ship after eleven years of silence—the deep-space vessel Vesper, presumed lost. Emotional beat: trembling hope curdling into dread when scans show life signs impossibly small.

chapters.title: Children of the Vesper
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Vesper lands; its crew has been aged backward to childhood by proximity to a temporal anomaly they charted. Emotional beat: horror and tenderness as Paloma realizes these are the colonists' own descendants.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ines Reyes, the Vesper's captain now a twelve-year-old with adult memories fraying like old film. She recognizes the beacon's design. Emotional beat: fierce disorientation and the terror of losing oneself.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Hides
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Deciphering Sol's code, Ines learns the beacon broadcasts a false uninhabitable-world signature to keep two rival fleets—the Concord and the Halcyon Combine—from claiming Meridian. Emotional beat: betrayal; their mission was never exploration but erasure.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma and Ines realize the beacon is decaying; within months it will fail and expose the garden. Emotional beat: shared burden forming the first real bond between them.

chapters.title: Sol's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A final coded entry reveals Sol died sealing the beacon's core, which can only be re-keyed by someone with her genetic imprint—or her memories. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, and dawning responsibility.

chapters.title: Small Hands, Old Eyes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The de-aged crew settles into the garden; Paloma becomes reluctant caretaker and teacher. Emotional beat: unexpected warmth, the garden finally serving someone.

chapters.title: The Concord's Wake
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A Concord scout ship passes at the system's edge; the beacon flickers and barely holds. Emotional beat: cold fear—time is shorter than they thought.

chapters.title: Lessons in Growing Things
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Teaching the child-crew botany, Paloma watches Ines remember more each day—and age slightly faster near the beacon. Emotional beat: love beginning, tangled with guilt over what proximity costs Ines.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Moon
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Intercepted traffic shows both fleets have scheduled survey passes in ninety days. The lie needs a new author. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into desperation.

chapters.title: Becoming Sol
chapters.summary: Paloma attempts to interface with the beacon using Sol's neural archive found in the garden's root vault. Emotional beat: violation and awe—Paloma glimpses Sol's memories and feels identity blur.

chapters.title: The Archive's Price
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Each sync with Sol's archive ages Paloma prematurely and erodes Paloma's own memories. Ines begs them to stop. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit—each would sacrifice self for the other.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Montage chapter: repairs, lessons, stolen moments in the seed vault. Emotional beat: fragile happiness built on a countdown.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers War
chapters.summary: Crew member Tomas, aged to seven, recalls the fleet battle his parents fled. His nightmares spread panic among the children. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The beacon begins echoing fragments of Sol's voice; the children believe she haunts the station. Emotional beat: superstition masking a technical truth—the core is waking.

chapters.title: What Paloma Forgot
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. After a deep sync, Paloma loses a full year of memories—including the first weeks with Ines. Emotional beat: heartbreak; Ines is a stranger to them again.

chapters.title: Falling Again
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines decides to make Paloma fall in love again rather than let them sacrifice themselves blind. Emotional beat: tender, deliberate courtship inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Halcyon Probe
chapters.summary: A Halcyon automated probe enters orbit. Paloma, half-merged with Sol's knowledge, spoofs a planetary collapse to turn it away. Emotional beat: triumph laced with horror at how easily they lied.

chapters.title: Sixty Days
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The spoof bought time but flagged attention; both fleets reroute survey ships. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Ines Grows
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Near the stabilizing beacon, Ines's body begins aging forward again—her mind and body converging toward thirty. Emotional beat: joy and fear; restoration means facing command decisions she once fled.

chapters.title: The Captain Returns
chapters.summary: Ines, now adult, formally takes command of the Vesper survivors. Paloma struggles to recognize the person they love. Emotional beat: identity shifting underfoot—love tested by change.

chapters.title: Sol's Confession
chapters.summary: Deep in the archive, Paloma finds Sol's true confession: she caused the temporal anomaly deliberately, trying to buy the colony time, and the Vesper was collateral. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—every savior here is also a saboteur.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Fleet vanguards arrive in-system. Ines proposes broadcasting the truth and negotiating; Paloma argues the lie still protects the children. Emotional beat: first real fracture between them.

chapters.title: The Vote in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The surviving crew votes: reveal or conceal. It ties; Ines breaks it toward revelation. Emotional beat: democracy's weight, and Paloma's wounded silence.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Discovering someone—Tomas, acting on nightmare-fear—has damaged the beacon to force early reveal, Paloma must repair it alone through a radiation storm. Emotional beat: fury dissolving into compassion for a frightened child.

chapters.title: Storm Work
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines walks out into the storm to help Paloma, nearly dying when the temporal field surges. Emotional beat: love proven in the flesh; they save each other and the beacon.

chapters.title: Twenty Days
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With the beacon stable but fleets inbound, Paloma accepts the vote. They begin composing the broadcast—a truth engineered to be survivable. Emotional beat: grim craftsmanship, hope as engineering.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The broadcast goes out: the garden exists, the anomaly is contained, Meridian offers sanctuary and food to both fleets' civilian populations. Emotional beat: terrifying exposure—the lie released like a bird.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Both fleets respond—not with diplomacy but with boarding parties racing for the beacon's control core. Emotional beat: betrayal of hope; power reaching for the lever.

chapters.title: The Core Room
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Concord and Halcyon officers confront each other inside the beacon chamber; Paloma stands between them, merged deeply enough with Sol to threaten collapsing the anomaly entirely. Emotional beat: the climax's held breath.

chapters.title: Mutually Assured Gardens
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines brokers the standoff: whoever controls the beacon controls the temporal weapon, so neither side can take it without the other destroying it. Emotional beat: deterrence born not of weapons but of a garden worth sparing.

chapters.title: Ceasefire at the Trellis
chapters.summary: Negotiations move to the greenhouse itself. The commanders' children, playing among the crops with the Vesper kids, do what diplomats cannot. Emotional beat: the theme made visible—power softened by living things.

chapters.title: The Price Paloma Paid
chapters.summary: Paloma collapses; the syncs have burned through most of their memories. Ines holds them, reciting their shared history back to them. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; identity held in another's keeping.

chapters.title: Replanting
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Recovery in the garden's medical bay; memories return in fragments, some Sol's, some their own, permanently braided. Emotional beat: acceptance of a composite self—identity as a garden, not a monument.

chapters.title: The Meridian Accords
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Both fleets sign accords making Meridian neutral ground governed by the colonists; the beacon becomes a lighthouse instead of a mask. Emotional beat: weary triumph, the corruption of power checked by shared stake.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Says Now
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma re-keys the beacon to broadcast the garden's real signature—an invitation. Ships begin arriving with soil, seeds, and settlers. Emotional beat: the garden finally for someone.

chapters.title: Ines Stays
chapters.summary: Ines resigns her commission, choosing Meridian over the fleet that made her. She and Paloma plant the first orchard together. Emotional beat: love chosen freely after duty is discharged.

chapters.title: Log 4,413
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing frame. Paloma writes the next entry in Sol's log, addressed to whoever tends the garden long after them; Ines adds a line in her own hand. Emotional beat: continuity, legacy, and peace—the signal carried forward.
